edible_parts: Young leaves and flowers (tea); flowers as a garnish.
other_uses: Late-season nectar and pollen for bees and migrating insects; Solidago is one of the highest-value native genera for supporting insect herbivores. Flowers yield a yellow to gold dye.
prep: Dry leaves and flowering tops for tea. Flowers can be battered and fried or scattered on food; the flavour is mildly anise-bitter.
harvest: Leaves early summer; flowering tops August–October.
sun: Part shade to full sun — unusually shade-tolerant for a goldenrod, at home on woodland edges.
soil: Dry to medium, well-drained; tolerates poor and rocky ground.
risks: Goldenrod pollen is heavy and insect-carried, so it is not a hay-fever cause (that is ragweed, which blooms at the same time). Avoid confusing with ragwort (Senecio), which is toxic.
buy: Regional native nurseries; occasionally in seed mixes for woodland edges.
